preamble: Glide formation turns the mid back vowel [o] into the labio-velar glide [w] when it stands before another vowel, resolving hiatus. The vowel raises to [+high] and becomes non-syllabic, so the sequence becomes a rising diphthong. It happened in Vulgar Latin (coāgulāre > *quaglāre, whence Spanish cuajar and Italian quaglio), it is productive across word boundaries in colloquial Chicano Spanish (lo habla [lwala]), and in Korean a stem-final o contracts with the infinitive ending -a into wa (보아 > 봐 [pwa]). Comparative work on hiatus resolution also reports o-gliding before non-round vowels in isiXhosa.

examples.note: In casual speech, word-final mid /o/ glides to [w] before a following vowel that differs from it in backness or height.

examples.from: tengo hipo /tengo # ipo/ 'I have the hiccups'

examples.note: The hiatus o.a became the rising diphthong [wa] after syncope; the learned doublet coagular keeps the hiatus.

examples.to: Late Latin quāglum > Italian quaglio (variant of caglio)
examples.note: Same gliding of o before a; the learned doublet coagulo keeps the hiatus.
The stem vowel /o/ becomes [w] before the ending /a/, giving the contracted infinitive.
Same contraction; the uncontracted form is not used.

sources: Baković, E. (2006). Hiatus resolution and incomplete identity. Rutgers Optimality Archive ROA-813. https://roa.rutgers.edu/files/813-0306/813-BAKOVIC-0-0.PDF
